wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the dispatcher is an in-process library API and the refusal contract is any raised client error, so a crash and a clean refusal are observationally identical; a fix that crashes on every delivery fails the functional suite (refuse_all.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the delivery route itself; there is no neighbouring resource whose authority could be substituted
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: deliveries have a single direction (TONAPI to the application) and no role or peer pair
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every delivery runs a handler and the tests assert that side effect, so a read-only guard cannot pass
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step sits between the presented credential and the check

traps.shape: a route the application registers with a custom path before provisioning; the dispatcher stores a secret only under the default suffix path, so the routing table accepts the custom route but verification is skipped

traps.realistic_because: the reported route; provisioning uses the default suffix while routing uses the registered route, so the two maps disagree

traps.shape: a route registered after provisioning: adding a handler resets the routing table but never issues a secret for the new route, so a delivery to it is dispatched unsigned
traps.where: pytonapi/webhook/dispatcher.py:258-260 and 341-343 (registration) with the lookup at 286-288

traps.realistic_because: the published fix's own far site: it changes the endpoints provisioning creates but a setup-only fix leaves cleanup looking for the old default endpoints

traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both enumerations truncate to handlers[0], so a fix that widens one without the other either strands a provisioned route or makes it reachable without its secret
